Hi Amelia — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we all have the same context:

Call highlights:
- StrataHealth is leaning toward a Private VPC deployment (data residency and audit requirements are the main drivers).
- Primary security concerns: egress control, tenant isolation, KMS integration, and audit log retention.
- You expressed a preference for a PrivateLink-style endpoint but wanted clarification on network architecture tradeoffs.

Action items for StrataHealth (please confirm):
1) Confirm timeline target for a production pilot (you mentioned Q3).
2) Provide primary network contact for technical deep dive (name/email).
3) Confirm whether StrataHealth will manage the egress allowlist on your side or prefer Redwood-managed egress e.g., via NAT/proxy.
4) Confirm KMS/HSM requirements and whether we should include our KMS integration checklist in the SOW.

What I will do:
- Attach a short Private VPC checklist (network-level asks + template allowlist) for your network team to fill out.
- Monica (cc'd) will own the technical deep dive and can run a 30-min session with your network/SRE to walk the template.
- I’ll open a HubSpot deal record and attach the procurement steps (DocuSign/order form, typical lead times).

Attachments: redwood-private-vpc-checklist.xlsx (checklist + allowlist template)

Proposed next step: 30-min network deep dive next week — please share two windows that work for Rajiv or your network lead and we’ll book.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Best,

Alex — thanks for the recap and the checklist. Confirming a few items from our side:

1) Timeline: Q3 pilot still looks right; goal to have networking and procurement cleared by end of Q2.
2) Network contact: Rajiv Kumar (rajiv.kumar@stratahealth.com) — he’s on netops and will join the deep dive.
3) Egress allowlist: StrataHealth prefers to maintain allowlists from our side (compliance requires us to control outbound rules). If Redwood can provide a static IP list or PrivateLink endpoint details that’s preferred.
4) KMS: We use an internal KMS (AWS KMS) and will need guidance on key wrapping/CMK usage and any HSM requirements.

Also, for security we’d prefer PrivateLink over classic VPC peering if it’s supported for the deployment mode you propose — reduces cross-VPC routing complexity for our auditors. Please include any limitations (regional availability, per-tenant endpoints, cost delta) in the deep dive.

Could you send the allowlist template as CSV? Rajiv prefers that format. Also can you attach the procurement/order flow (DocuSign) so our procurement team has visibility?

Thanks,
Amelia Barnes
Sr. Program Manager, Product Security

Subject: Private VPC network deep-dive materials + allowlist CSV

Hi Amelia / Rajiv — thanks for confirming Rajiv as the netops lead. Per Alex’s note, attaching the CSV allowlist template and a short technical checklist to help the 30-min session be efficient.

Summary of what I’ll cover in the call (and what we need completed to scope the private deployment):
- PrivateLink vs VPC peering: short pros/cons (PrivateLink = endpoint per-region, narrower exposure; Peering = easier routing but more cross-VPC access to consider). We’ll share regional availability for PrivateLink during the call.
- Egress model: because you handle allowlists, we’ll provide the per-region egress IPs and the service FQDNs. If you instead want Redwood-managed egress we can discuss NAT/proxy options and service-level isolation.
- KMS integration: we support both customer-managed CMKs (AWS KMS) and Redwood-managed keys. If you choose CMK, we’ll walk through key policy requirements and rotation windows.
- Audit logs & retention: we’ll outline the logs we surface (request metadata, model versions, token counts) and export options to your SIEM.

Attached: network-allowlist-template.csv (CSV schema for IP/CIDR, port ranges, expected traffic patterns)
Reference: redwood-private-vpc-checklist.xlsx (original checklist Alex sent)
Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cREDWOOD-STRATA-NETWORK-SHARED

Availability: I can run the deep dive on either of the times Alex suggested. Please confirm which slot works and we’ll send an invite.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
